findings.finding: Current integrated model uses EUR378,850 corporate Part 1 and EUR414,550 total revenue. Parent confirmed the earlier EUR381,350 mention was superseded. The monthly original-source calculation supports the current EUR378,850 figure.
findings.action: Use the hashed current model; rerun this challenge if numerical assumptions or arrays change.

findings.finding: The source states an internal senior exists, but the fixed payroll line is called delivery coordination. Internal fee savings EUR50,757.60 rely on treating that salary as already in EUR2,500/month and assuming the senior can teach allocated programs. The new EUR150 gross allowance/day plus 25% load and EUR1,000 February preparation are explicit proposed costs, not source prices or proof of teaching capability.
findings.action: Disclose payroll coverage, eligible course roster, preparation objective and skill review. Keep supplier cover until the senior and customer approve each allocation. If eligibility fails, revert affected days to external fees.

findings.finding: January needs 15.8 external lead days and February needs 16, including the new February course. Six–eight weeks notice puts January reservations in November/December 2025 and February mostly December/early January. No prior bookings are supplied. A new late-February course can fit a six-week January start; an eight-week lead or late January decision moves it into March.
findings.action: Declare January opening-pipeline/external reservation condition and a specific late-February date with at least six weeks confirmed notice. If not secured, move February event and revenue to March; do not call an unbooked trainer guaranteed.

findings.finding: The calendar needs 19 assistant person-days annually, including 9 person-days from additional people due to simultaneous positions. September needs three distinct assistants for two days: regular covers one position, two additional assistants cover four person-days. Aggregate monthly excess over four days is only two and understates concurrency.
findings.action: Book extra people April 1 day, June 2 days, September two people × 2 days, November 2 days; use six–eight-week calendar controls. Their ordinary fees are already costed; do not add them twice. Exact program dates may expose further cross-event overlap.

findings.finding: The four extra courses use currently unserved pooled enquiries, adding 55 seats and EUR33,000 revenue at EUR600/seat. Historical pooled conversion is not price-specific proof that all enquiries buy this premium course. Marketing budget remains unchanged except EUR1,000 January setup; existing campaign resources must be allocated to the four dates.
findings.action: Name the course promotion owner, ring-fence existing promotional effort, explain why four groups will pay EUR600, and use pre-registration thresholds. Do not claim generic enquiry counts are guaranteed demand or silently rely on additional paid promotion.

findings.finding: Part 2 has 162.18 expected lead days, 91.68 internal and 70.50 external. Fractional program/day amounts are valid probability-weighted budget expectations. They are not executable reservations. Monthly upward rounding requires at least 73 external whole days, plus 92 internal days, within stated limits; real one-/two-day program groupings and overlaps can require more.
findings.action: Maintain a dated whole-program calendar and reserve external day blocks before accepting each delivery. The two-day internal reserve helps preparation/quality but does not guarantee unlimited external capacity.

findings.finding: EUR232.8125 residual travel/day comes from the current 26-event program register, not historic actual travel. Applying 25% employer cost to variable internal allowances is a conservative new management assumption; the original 25% instruction explicitly refers to fixed salaries.
findings.action: Call travel a register-based proxy and allowance burden a proposed planning assumption. Keep both visible for sensitivity testing.

findings.finding: The integrated Part 2 improves operating result by EUR72,815.1625, but still loses EUR19,745.8271. It does not meet a positive-profit objective. Most improvement comes from internal fee savings rather than a proven sales uplift.
findings.action: Recommend the operating controls conditionally, report the remaining loss plainly, and set a further board review before committing additional growth or capital. Do not describe this budget as profitable.

internalAllocationFailsAllDays.assumption: All internal allocated days revert to external rates; fixed salary remains; preparation cost already spent.

internalSeniorSalaryNotAlreadyIncluded.assumption: Scenario only: an additional EUR2,500 gross monthly senior salary with 25% planning burden is needed March–December. Not a claim that such a hire or missing salary is evidenced.

tenPercentCorporateRevenueShortfallWithB.assumption: Conservative downside: instructor/venue capacity, payroll, materials preparation, travel and all other delivery costs remain committed; only ordinary 5% sales commission and additional Anna contract premium fall proportionately. This is a stress scenario, not a recomputed lower-volume cost budget.

oneFewerSeatAtEveryExistingAndNewOpenDat.assumption: Lead/venue days unchanged; only materials and 5% ordinary commission change.

sixSeatsAtEachNewPremiumCourse.assumption: Four new events still run, fixed lead/venue days unchanged, contribution per lost seat EUR540.

verdict: Arithmetic and monthly capacity limits pass for the hashed model. Feasible as a conditional expected budget with the disclosed assumptions and reservation controls; remaining loss and internal allocation uncertainty must be explicit.
